The Florida Department of Children and Families (Department), Office of Community Services, is issuing this Request for Applications (RFA) to procure direct services under Florida's Responsible Fatherhood Initiative. This RFA establishes a coordinated statewide framework for the delivery of Responsible Fatherhood Initiative services through the following program components: Comprehensive Needs of Fathers (CNF); Responsible Fatherhood Education Program (RFEP); and Mentorship Programs for At-Risk Male Students (MPARMS). Applicants may propose one, two, or all three program components within one or more judicial circuits. The Department encourages integrated service delivery and collaboration among program components to improve outcomes for fathers, families, and at-risk male youth.

description: MFMP MFMP for Vendors Vendor Disclosures State of Florida Advertisements Invitation to Bid Invitation to Bid: BDC09-26-27 Sebastian Inlet - Water Holding Tank Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) Advertisement Status: OPEN Last Edit Date/Time: 10/02/2026, 12:52 PM Advertisement Number: ITB-17132 Agency Advertisement Number: BDC09-26/27 Version Number: 1 Published Date/Time: 10/02/2026 12:52 PM Start Date/Time: 10/02/2026 12:52 PM End Date/Time: 10/27/2026 07:30 PM Commodity Codes Code Description 72151101 Septic system construction service 72151102 Fire sprinkler system installation service 72152800 Water well drilling services 72152801 Domestic water well drilling service 72154055 Tank cleaning service 72154056 Tank maintenance or repair service NOTICE OF INVITATION TO BID STATE OF FLORIDA DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION BID NO. BDC09-26/27 The Department of Environmental Protection, Bureau of Design and Construction is soliciting formal, competitive, sealed bids from Contractors licensed to work in the jurisdiction for the project listed below. PROJECT NAME: Sebastian Inlet State Park – Water Holding Tank BID SUBMITTAL DUE DATE: No later than 3:30 pm (ET), Tuesday, October 27, 2026, to the below address: Florida Department of Environmental Protection, Bureau of Design and Construction, 3800 Commonwealth Boulevard, MS #520, Tallahassee, Florida, 32399-3000, Attention: Alisha Sadler, Bureau of Design and Construction, (850) 245-3127. (For hand delivery: Carr Building, Welcome Desk.) The Department reserves the right to reject any or all bids. BID POSTING DATE: No later than 3:30 pm (ET), Tuesday, November 3, 2026, unless extended by the Department for good cause. INSTRUCTIONS: Documents for this bid will be available for download on Friday, October 2, 2026. Any firm desiring a Project Manual with the plans for this project may obtain directions by emailing BDC_Contracts@dep.state.fl.us. SCOPE OF WORK: Base Bid: Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, supervision and permitting per the contract documents. Note: Bidder Prequalification is required for all bids. Each bidder shall provide a copy of its biennial pre-qualification letter from FDEP’s Bureau of Design and Construction. To request a pre-qualification letter, the bidder should email BDC_Contracts@dep.state.fl.us. description: MFMP MFMP for Vendors Vendor Disclosures State of Florida Advertisements Invitation to Bid Patterson Loop 26/27 Timber Sale Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (FDACS) Advertisement Status: OPEN Last Edit Date/Time: 10/08/2026, 12:12 PM Advertisement Number: ITB-17186 Agency Advertisement Number: Version Number: 1 Published Date/Time: 10/08/2026 12:12 PM Start Date/Time: 10/08/2026 12:12 PM End Date/Time: 10/28/2026 02:00 PM Responses Open Date/Time: 10/28/2026 02:00 PM Commodity Codes Code Description 93141904 Agricultural or rural cooperatives services SALE ADVERTISEMENT Patterson Loop 26/27 Timber Sale The Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services, Florida Forest Service is seeking sealed bids for the sale of timber. Patterson Loop 26/27 Timber Sale in its entirety spans 254 acres. It is estimated to yield 1,427 tons of pine pulpwood/mulch wood and 165 tons of eucalyptus pulpwood/mulch wood. Broken down by species, this is a per unit sale thinning of approximately 220 acres of planted south Florida slash pine, and a clearcutting of approximately 34 acres of planted eucalyptus in Okaloacoochee Slough State Forest in Hendry County, Florida (see attached maps). These maps, and this project in general, divide the harvest into four separate areas referred to as Areas 1, 2, 3, and 4, corresponding to the stands proceeding West to East. The pine sale areas (Areas 1 and 4) are comprised of 19-23-year-old south Florida slash in the range of 200-400 trees per acre calculated through a range of 5-to-7-inch DBH. Timber available for harvest in Areas 1 and 4 include a 3rd row thinning with selection includes diseased, deformed, defective, forked, and suppressed trees. Both pine sale areas will have a target BA of 30 or higher post-harvest. The two smaller stands totaling 34 acres of planted eucalyptus plantations (Areas 2 and 3) were last clearcut 25 years ago. Areas 2 and 3 will be a clearcut. All areas will require low ground pressure equipment. Sale boundaries are roads, wetlands, fire lines or obvious timber type changes. This will be an eighteen (18) month contract. Interested parties may obtain complete bid information by contacting James Kavanagh at (239) 690-8031. The Florida Forest Service reserves the right to reject any and all bids and to waive any irregularity in bids received. Bids will be opened at: 10941 Palm Beach Blvd, Fort Myers, Fl 33905 10/28/2026 10:00 AM, EDT

title: Actuarial Services for the Stanley G. Tate Florida Prepaid College Program
description: MFMP MFMP for Vendors Vendor Disclosures State of Florida Advertisements Invitation to Negotiate Actuarial Services for the Stanley G. Tate Florida Prepaid College Program State Board of Administration (SBA) Advertisement Status: OPEN Last Edit Date/Time: 10/22/2026, 02:29 PM Advertisement Number: ITN-17258 Agency Advertisement Number: ITN 26-02 Version Number: 4 Published Date/Time: 10/14/2026 03:28 PM Start Date/Time: 10/14/2026 08:00 PM End Date/Time: 04/30/2027 12:00 PM Commodity Codes Code Description 80101512 Actuarial consulting services The Prepaid Plan requires independent actuarial analysis supporting the Board’s statutory duty to evaluate the actuarial soundness of the prepaid fund and to establish plan prices (See Appendix D for an overall description of the program). The services below are minimum requirements; the selected Respondent will perform them using data and assumptions supplied or approved by the Board and in accordance with applicable actuarial standards. 3.01(1) Transition Plan Submit and maintain an orderly transition plan, if applicable. The transition plan should describe the process, details, and schedule for providing an orderly transition from the current provider. The objectives of the transition plan should be to minimize the impacts on continuity of operations, maintain communication with staff, identify key issues, and overcome barriers to transition. 3.01(2) Annual Planning Meet in person with Board staff at least annually to plan the next 12 months of deliverables. As part of annual planning, review material Program experience, assumptions that may warrant further review, emerging actuarial issues, and potential analytical needs that may support significant Board policy, financial, or Program decisions. Provide a detailed annual work plan identifying Board data needs, delivery dates, review points, meetings, draft and final deliverables, and dependencies necessary to meet the Board’s schedule. 3.01(3) Data Review The Board will provide all data necessary to perform the specified contract services. Quarterly, the Actuary shall review, load, reconcile, and evaluate Board-provided data; investigate anomalies; determine whether information is complete and adequate; and recommend data improvements needed for valuations, pricing, and experience studies. (See Appendix I for an example data file). The selected Respondent shall protect Board data and use appropriate actuarial and statistical systems to perform and document all analyses. 3.01(4) Quarterly Actuarial Valuations and Cash Flows Prepare four quarterly actuarial valuation letters each year, as of June 30, September 30, December 31, and March 31, using the latest experience data, Board-approved assumptions, and anticipated future years of sales (as directed by the Board). Reports should include information, charts, breakdowns, and explanations in sufficient detail for the Board to understand the actuarial position of the Prepaid Plan. In addition, monthly undiscounted and discounted cash flows shall be provided to support the appropriate values in the report. See Appendix F for an example of a quarterly valuation report. 3.01(5) Annual Actuarial Valuation and Cash Flows Prepare one annual actuarial valuation report as of June 30. The report will update actuarial projections, include requested sensitivity analyses, reconcile surplus, review experience, recommend assumption changes when 4 appropriate, provide the program termination liability as provided for in Section 1009.98(8) Florida Statutes and with Board guidance, and provide projected undiscounted and discounted monthly cash flows. The Respondent shall review and analyze at least one major actuarial valuation assumption each year. See Appendix G for an example of an Annual Actuarial Adequacy Report NOTE: The annual actuarial adequacy review treats the Program as closed for valuation purposes, evaluating existing contracts without assuming any future sales. This approach does not mean the Program is closed to new purchases. Because the Program continues to sell plans each year, the quarterly actuarial reviews include estimated additional years of sales, as directed by the Board, and the associated future receipts and obligations. The resulting quarterly cash flow projections are used to construct the liability-driven investment (LDI) benchmark, aligning the investment strategy with projected net cash flows from both existing contracts and anticipated future sales. 3.01(6) Sensitivities Develop with the Board and periodically update a sensitivity matrix for material actuarial drivers. Where reasonably practicable, present the results in a form that helps staff understand the directional and approximate effect of defined changes on actuarial adequacy, projected cash flows, and plan pricing, together with appropriate limitations. 3.01(7) Annual Plan Pricing Prepare one annual Prepaid Plan pricing report each year for the designated enrollment period (currently July 1 through June 30), including plan prices by payment option and beneficiary age for each offered product. Test price adequacy, determine and disclose break-even rates of return, and provide illustrative prices at alternative inflation assumptions upon request. The Respondent shall review and analyze at least one major pricing assumption each year. See Appendix H for an example of the Annual Plan Pricing. 3.01(8) Supporting Files Provide electronic actuarial and pricing reports and usable supporting files, including payoff factors and projected cash flows, sufficient for Program operations, benchmark development, review of Board inputs and assumptions, and understanding of results. 3.01(9) Board Presentations and Consultation Appear before the Board annually, to explain and substantiate the annual actuarial adequacy and pricing reports. Consult with Board staff by letter, telephone, electronic communication, or in person upon request. 3.01(10) Professional Standards and Quality Control Perform all services in accordance with applicable qualification standards, Actuarial Standards of Practice, and the Actuarial Code of Professional Conduct. Maintain documented review and quality-control procedures for all deliverables. 3.01(11) Continuity Maintain a continuity plan, update it, and provide it to the Board annually, and cross-train personnel to preserve knowledge of the Prepaid Program. 5 3.01(12) Data Security and Confidentiality Maintain appropriate controls for confidential Board data, limit access to authorized personnel, use secure transmission and storage methods, and promptly report any incident affecting Board information. 3.01(13) Records, Documentation, and Audit Support Maintain work papers, models, assumptions, data reconciliations, and supporting documentation sufficient to reproduce and explain conclusions and to support Board oversight, audit, and transition to a successor provider. 3.01(14) Coordination and Responsiveness Coordinate with Board staff and other Board service providers, respond promptly to questions, identify emerging issues, and communicate any matter that may affect the accuracy, quality, or timeliness of deliverables. 3.01(15) Additional Actuarial Reports, Letters, or Assumption Studies At the Board’s request, conduct additional actuarial adequacy reports or letters, pricing reports or letters, or assumption studies. 3.01(16) Additional Actuarial Advisor Studies and Services At the Board’s request, and subject to advance written scope and fee approval, conduct additional sensitivity analyses, single-plan pricing analyses, or other special actuarial projects not identified above. 3.01(17) Workshops At the Board’s request, prepare and present an in-person workshop on calculations, data, assumptions, legislative changes, reporting, or improvements to models and methods. 3.01(18) Representation At the Board’s request, represent the Board before governing authorities on actuarial matters. 3.01(19) Legislation At the Board’s request, assist with preparation or review of legislation, fiscal notes, and bill analyses. 3.01(20) Other Value-Added Services Respondents may propose actuarial tools, dashboards, modeling enhancements, training, benchmarking, process improvements, or other services that provide additional value, efficiency, transparency, or risk reduction to the Board. Note: Illustrative annual adequacy, quarterly valuation, and pricing reports are informational and do not limit the Board’s ability to modify requirements during negotiations.

description: MFMP MFMP for Vendors Vendor Disclosures State of Florida Advertisements Single Source LIMS Maintenance & Technical Support Services Department of Law Enforcement (FDLE) Advertisement Status: OPEN Last Edit Date/Time: 10/06/2026, 04:51 PM Advertisement Number: SS-17153 Agency Advertisement Number: FDLE-SS-2706 Version Number: 1 Published Date/Time: 10/06/2026 04:51 PM Start Date/Time: 10/06/2026 04:51 PM End Date/Time: 10/27/2026 05:00 PM Commodity Codes Code Description 81112200 Software maintenance and support 81112211 Enterprise resource planning software maintenance Maintenance and support of the Florida Department of Law Enforcement’s (FDLE) Forensic Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) that provides evidence tracking, inventory, and auditing capabilities. This system accommodates multi-discipline services, including but not limited to Biology, Firearms, Chemistry and Toxicology. The current LIMS was acquired through competitive solicitation (RFP B1011) from Porter Lee Corporation in 2007 and is an essential element in maintaining FDLE Regional laboratories forensic accreditation standards. Since initial implementation, FDLE has acquired additional modules for the LIMS system, including the investigation’s Evidence Management System, Radio Frequency Identification System, .Net LIMS System, Toxicology Automation Module, Prelog v2, Android Software for Custody Transfer and Inventory Modules, as well as the Biology Automation Module. The purpose of this single source request is to request that FDLE continues to receive system maintenance and support services required for FDLE’s existing Laboratory Information Management System and Evidence Management System, Radio Frequency Identification System, Criminal Evidence Intake Module, .Net LIMS System, Toxicology Automation Module, Prelog v2, Android Software for Custody Transfer and Inventory Modules, and Biology Automation Module. This system maintenance is critical to ensure that FDLE continues to meet business needs and national forensic laboratory standards.

For licensing, contact: Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation Tallahassee, Florida 32399-0797 (850) 487-1395 NOTE: In accordance with section 287.057(23), Florida Statutes, respondents to this solicitation or persons acting on their behalf may not contact, between the release of the solicitation and the end of the 72-hour period following the agency posting the notice of intended award, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and state holidays, any employee or officer of the executive or legislative branch concerning any aspect of this solicitation, except in writing to the procurement officer or as provided in the solicitation documents. Violation of this provision may be grounds for rejecting a response. Public Meeting Notices and Meeting Agendas: Notice of the public meetings scheduled for this solicitation is provided in the timeline of the attached solicitation, with agendas for the public meetings. MFMP Transaction Fee: All payment(s) to the vendor(s) resulting from the contract(s) established by this competitive solicitation WILL be subject to the MFMP Transaction Fee unless the transaction is exempt from the Transaction Fee pursuant to Rule 60A-1.032, Florida Administrative Code. Scrutinized Companies Lists: Section 287.135, Florida Statutes, prohibits agencies from contracting with companies, for goods or services over $1,000,000, that are on either the Scrutinized Companies with Activities in Sudan List or the Scrutinized Companies with Activities in the Iran Petroleum Energy Sector List. Both lists are created pursuant to section 215.473, Florida Statutes. A vendor on either Scrutinized List may not bid on, submit a proposal for, or enter into or renew a contract for commodities and/or contractual services of $1 million or more. and 49 CFR Part 21; The Uniform Relocation Assistance and Real Property Acquisition Policies Act of 1970, (42 U.S.C. § 4601), (prohibits unfair treatment of persons displaced or whose property has been acquired because of Federal or Federal-aid programs and projects); Federal-Aid Highway Act of 1973, (23 U.S.C. § 324 et seq.), (prohibits discrimination on the basis of sex); Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, (29 U.S.C. § 794 et seq.), as amended, (prohibits discrimination on the basis of disability); and 49 CFR Part 27; The Age Discrimination Act of 1975, as amended, (42 U.S.C. § 6101 et seq.), (prohibits discrimination on the basis of age); Airport and Airway Improvement Act of 1982, (49 USC § 471, Section 47123), as amended, (prohibits discrimination based on race, creed, color, national origin, or sex); The Civil Rights Restoration Act of 1987, (PL 100-209), (Broadened the scope, coverage and applicability of Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, The Age Discrimination Act of 1975 and Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, by expanding the definition of the terms “programs or activities” to include all of the programs or activities of the Federal-aid recipients, sub-recipients and contractors, whether such programs or activities are Federally funded or not); Titles II and III of the Americans with Disabilities Act, which prohibit discrimination on the basis of disability in the operation of public entities, public and private transportation systems, places of public accommodation, and certain testing entities (42 U.S.C. §§ 12131 -- 12189) as implemented by Department of Transportation regulations at 49 C.F.R. parts 37 and 38; The Federal Aviation Administration’s Non-discrimination statute (49 U.S.C. § 47123) (prohibits discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, and sex); Executive Order 12898, Federal Actions to Address Environmental Justice in Minority Populations and Low-Income Populations, which ensures non-discrimination against minority populations by discouraging programs, policies, and activities with disproportionately high and adverse human health or environmental effects on minority and low-income populations; Executive Order 13166, Improving Access to Services for Persons with Limited English Proficiency, and resulting agency guidance, national origin discrimination includes discrimination because of limited English proficiency (LEP). To ensure compliance with Title VI, you must take reasonable steps to ensure that LEP persons have meaningful access to your programs (70 Fed. Reg. at 74087 to 74100); Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972, as amended, which prohibits you from discriminating because of sex in education programs or activities (20 U.S.C. 1681 et seq). In accordance with the ITB (including Section 21 of the ITB Solicitation Document), the Department reserves the right to cancel this ITB at any time prior to the Department’s execution of the Contract, without incurring any cost obligations or liabilities. The Department hereby provides notice of its decision to make no award and to reject all Bids received for DOT-ITB-27-8008-MB, Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) Replacement North Region, with the intent to resolicit. Failure to file a protest within the time prescribed in Section 120.57(3), Florida Statutes, or failure to post the bond or other security required by law within the time allowed for filing a bond shall constitute a waiver of proceedings under Chapter 120, Florida Statutes. title: Coldwater 2026 Salvage Sale
agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (FDACS)
description: MFMP MFMP for Vendors Vendor Disclosures State of Florida Advertisements Invitation to Bid Coldwater 2026 Salvage Sale Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (FDACS) Advertisement Status: OPEN Last Edit Date/Time: 10/22/2026, 03:56 PM Advertisement Number: ITB-17300 Agency Advertisement Number: Version Number: 1 Published Date/Time: 10/22/2026 03:56 PM Start Date/Time: 10/22/2026 03:56 PM End Date/Time: 10/29/2026 02:00 PM Commodity Codes Code Description 93141904 Agricultural or rural cooperatives services SALE ADVERTISEMENT Coldwater 2026 Salvage Sale The Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services, Florida Forest Service is seeking sealed bids for the sale of timber. This is a salvage harvest of merchantable pine and hardwood timber that has been damaged by Hurricane Isaias on October 9, 2026, on Blackwater River State Forest in Santa Rosa County, Florida (SFI Certified Forest BVC-SFIFM-700005). Within the total area of 18,628 acres, Florida Forest Service staff have identified areas of extensive damage which may be identified on the attached maps and/or identified while harvesting is ongoing. Substantial damage areas will be the highest priority for harvesting and must be cut before lower damage areas. Approximately 1,727 acres surrounding red cockaded woodpecker clusters will also be prioritized and must be cut before March 15, 2027. The successful bidder must begin harvesting within 10 business days of contract execution. There is no volume estimate for this sale. Products include salvage pine pulpwood, salvage pine chip-n-saw, salvage pine sawtimber, and salvage hardwood pulpwood. All timber which is blown down, broken off, leaning more than 15 degrees, or otherwise damaged is available for harvest. Timber that does not meet these criteria may only be harvested by approval of the Forester-in-Charge. Sale boundaries will consist of roads, wetlands, forest boundaries, recreational sites, and any timber type changes or undamaged areas. This salvage is being advertised at the same time as the West Boundary 2026 Salvage Sale and Wolfe Creek 2026 Salvage Sale. In the event that the same bidder places the highest acceptable bid on multiple sales, the successful bidder must forfeit all but one sale to the next highest bidder to allow for a faster response or have adequate equipment and personnel to harvest multiple sales simultaneously. This will be a six (6) month contract. Interested parties may obtain complete bid information by contacting Eric Howell at (850) 957-5725. The Florida Forest Service reserves the right to reject any and all bids and to waive any irregularity in bids received. Bids will be opened at: 11650 Munson Highway, Milton, Fl 32570 10/29/2026 10:00 AM, CDT

title: University of Florida - GradHaus
description: MFMP MFMP for Vendors Vendor Disclosures State of Florida Advertisements Invitation to Negotiate University of Florida - GradHaus University of Florida Advertisement Status: OPEN Last Edit Date/Time: 10/23/2026, 12:34 PM Advertisement Number: ITN-17296 Agency Advertisement Number: ITN2026-104 Version Number: 2 Published Date/Time: 10/22/2026 08:34 PM Start Date/Time: 10/22/2026 08:34 PM End Date/Time: 11/19/2026 10:00 PM Commodity Codes Code Description 80131500 Lease and rental of property or building Summary: The user of the proposed leased area is the University of Florida’s College of the Arts, GradHaus (Graduate Research in Art Development). All uses are for academic research and artistic practice in areas such as art + technology, ceramics, creative photography, drawing, painting, printmaking, and sculpture (students create artwork using a variety of materials) and related uses as necessary for operation. Tenant seeks a location to facilitate student art studios, collaboration, and meeting space. A roll-up loading door/dock with adequate access and parking. Access hours are generally Monday-Friday 8:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m., but Tenant will need access after-hours and on weekends Additional Requirements and/or Limitations: The proposed Premises should include approximately 6,500-8,500 usable square feet to be reflected as rentable square feet for leasing purposes. The location desired is within a radius of 2 miles from the center of UF main campus and further defined in Exhibit “C” attached. Proposed locations outside of the defined area will be considered on a case-by-case basis. Delineation of space: The proposed premises should be relatively close to the general layout presented below. Square footages are estimates and dimensions do not have to be exact. Final space requirements may vary from the details below: Secured Area – A minimum of: • Concrete or other easy-care flooring. • 25 individual, open-to-structure, partitioned, design studio spaces of various sizes ranging from approximately 100 - 200 USF each. • 2 Administrative/advanced skill offices (approximately 180-250 USF each). • Graduate student open/lecture area to accommodate 8-10 students. Ideally the open spaces would be free of load bearing columns or walls that restrict movement or visual fields (approximately 1,000 USF). • Industrial sink and wash area with plumbing to accommodate use thereof. • Eye wash station. • 1 Break room/area (approximately 300-400 USF) with sink, cabinets, and room for a full-size refrigerator, table and microwave. • 1 Storage room (approximately 100-150 USF). • Parking spaces, user prefers at least 25 spaces with a minimum of 15 spaces (may be allocated and nonexclusive), approximately 4:1,000 SF. • 2 handicap accessible restroom(s) of adequate size to accommodate an office of this size. • Industrial level ventilation system. • Ability to store flammable materials in a Flammable Safety Cabinet. Timing: Occupancy is desired by May 1st, 2028.

title: Gulf to Lake 26/27 Timber Sale
agency: Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (FDACS)
description: MFMP MFMP for Vendors Vendor Disclosures State of Florida Advertisements Invitation to Bid Gulf to Lake 26/27 Timber Sale Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (FDACS) Advertisement Status: OPEN Last Edit Date/Time: 10/23/2026, 02:12 PM Advertisement Number: ITB-17306 Agency Advertisement Number: Version Number: 1 Published Date/Time: 10/23/2026 02:12 PM Start Date/Time: 10/23/2026 02:12 PM End Date/Time: 11/12/2026 03:00 PM Commodity Codes Code Description 93141904 Agricultural or rural cooperatives services SALE ADVERTISEMENT Gulf to Lake 26/27 Timber Sale The Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services, Florida Forest Service is seeking sealed bids for the sale of timber. This sale is a clearcut of approximately 153 acres of sand pine from the Citrus Tract of Withlacoochee State Forest located in Citrus County, Florida (see attached maps). The sale area consists of natural and planted sand pine. Any longleaf pine that occurs within the sale boundary is not included in the sale and must not be harvested. Due to planned management activities, harvest boundaries are categorized as either Primary or Contingency. The Primary Area is approximately 138 acres in size. Timber available for harvest includes all sand pine timber within the Primary Area. The Contingency Area is approximately 15 acres in size. Harvesting in this area will only be approved if the timing of the harvest does not interfere with management activities (e.g. prescribed burning). Any harvesting in the Contingency Area will be at the direction of the Forester-in-Charge. The estimated volume for this sale is 7,347 tons of pine pulpwood/mulch wood. Of the total tons 6,627 tons are included in the Primary Area and 720 tons are included in the Contingency Area. The sale boundary is designated by distinct stand type change, roads, fire lines, and/or orange painted boundary trees. The length of this contract is for twelve (12) months. Interested parties may obtain complete bid information by contacting Genevieve Montgomery at (352) 382-0967. The Florida Forest Service reserves the right to reject any and all bids and to waive any irregularity in bids received. Bids will be opened at: 15019 Broad Street, Brooksville, Fl 34601 11/12/2026 10:00 AM, EST
